land.text: Murom and Ryazan, bequeathed with Chernigov in 1054: 'In 1127, it became a separate principality and was known as the Principality of Murom-Ryazan'

predecessors.note: The infobox lists Kievan Rus' as predecessor. Ryazan's dossier (Cliopatria row from 1094) draws the same land as Ryazan; the renderer must carve Murom out of it.

land.text: 'In 1392, Vasily I of Moscow obtained a patent from Tokhtamysh authorizing the annexation of the Murom principality'

capitals.name: Murom
capitals.note: Infobox capital Murom; the page records no capital move.

correction.text: the core of the principality, 'primarily concentrated along the tributaries of the Oka'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (no Cliopatria row). The page gives no area and no boundary, only 'the tributaries of the Oka' with Gorokhovets to the north-west and the Pra to the west; an 80 km radius round Murom is my reading. 1127-1129 it was the joint Murom-Ryazan principality; Ryazan's own Cliopatria shape (1094-1240) overlaps this land.

region.text: the core of the principality, 'primarily concentrated along the tributaries of the Oka'

ledger.note: 1127: Murom-Ryazan becomes a separate principality under Yaroslav Sviatoslavich. 'In 1127, it became a separate principality'; 'The youngest, Yaroslav, ruled in Murom and Ryazan from 1127.' Year and name are the page's; the land is my reading. After his death in 1129 his sons received Murom and Ryazan respectively.

region.text: the core of the principality, 'primarily concentrated along the tributaries of the Oka'

ledger.note: 1392: Moscow annexes Murom. 'In 1392, Vasily I of Moscow obtained a patent from Tokhtamysh authorizing the annexation of the Murom principality' (the same patent covered Nizhny Novgorod and Gorodets).

wars.name: Mongol invasion of Rus (Murom, 1237-1238)
wars.outcome: 'Murom was destroyed or at least devastated by the Mongol invasion of 1237-1238'; ravaged again in 1283 and 1293. The page records no change of border or status, so no zone.
wars.note: The prince of Murom 'continued to be a firm ally of the grand prince of Vladimir'; after 1257 the principality 'carried on independently'.

certainty.note: No survey or treaty line; only the Oka tributaries and the neighbours named on the page.

sources.title: Principality of Murom
sources.note: Infobox 1127-1392, Murom-Ryazan, the 1237-1238 devastation, the 1353-1355 succession, the 1392 patent; no area.

notes: New state (Cliopatria has no Murom row); flagged by eu-16-b and eu-16-c as a counterpart. One page only (page budget; the article is short). Not settled: the extent of the principality (the page gives none), the date Murom and Ryazan separated for good (1129 seats, mid-12th century per the page), the princely list (the page contradicts itself on Yury Yaroslavich 1129-1143 versus Sviatoslav and Rostislav). The moscow dossier says Moscow 'also took Murom' without a year; this page gives 1392. Ryazan's Cliopatria shape (1094-1240) already covers Murom; the colour agent and the renderer must carve this dossier's region out of it. Wikidata id unknown (wikidata.org unreachable).
